To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transition from squamous to spindle cell morphology in a series of mouse skin tumors is recessive at the level of cell morphology and lack expression of differentiation proteins, and that the loss of these properties in the hybrids is associated with loss of tumorigenic potential.

the conversion of mouse skin carcinomas from a squamous to a spindle cell phenotype is a recessive process, and that loss of the cell adhe- sion molecule E-cad- herin and the desmoplakin protein is an early event in this conversion.

the conversion of mouse skin tumors to spindle cell tumors is a recessive phenomenon and that it involves loss of a gene which controls the expression of keratin and other epithelial cell differentiation markers, and the acquisition of a fibrobastoid morphology.

the genetic changes which underlie the transition to a more malignant and metastatic phenotype in mouse skin tumors, and the role played by the cell surface proteins E-cadherins and desmoplakins in the maintenance of the squamous phenotype and suppression of metastatic behavior.
understanding the genetic basis of the transition from premalignant to malignant phenotypes in skin cancer and the mechanisms by which malignant cells become metastatic.
the genetic changes involved in mouse skin tumorigenesis and the role of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes in this process.

the spindle cell carcinoma is a recessive trait in mouse skin carcinogenesis.
the conversion of mouse skin carcinomas to spindle cells is a recessive genetic event.

spindle cell carcinomas arise from squamous carcinomas by a recessive process, which involves loss of the expression of cell surface adhesion molecules, destabilization of keratin filaments and loss of the ability of the cells to maintain their epithelial morphology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conversion of mouse skin papillomas to spindle cell carcinoma is a recessive, multistep event involving loss of the cell adhesions proteins, E-cad and Dpl and loss of keratins.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the spindle cell morphology is not a marker of malignancy, but rather reflects loss of a gene which is important for epithelial differentiation.
it is not the loss of a specific gene but rather the loss of the entire genetic information that is responsible for the spindle cell transformation.
the spindle cell conversion in mouse skin cancer is recessive, and is a late event in tumor progression, which occurs after the tumor has become highly malignant.
